symptom: The nightly goes red on the Mendix 11.15.0 and 11.16.0 legs (ako/mxcli run 46132208195, mendixlabs/mxcli run 46132550380), in `TestTestAttach_KeepsTheHostingAppsPageBundles`: `mxcli test --attach` exits 1 with `this change compiles to other Java classes, which the running runtime cannot load without a restart, and --attach cannot restart it`, although the attach only injects a test microflow. 10.24, 11.6, 11.12, 11.13, 11.14 and 11.17 are green
cause: The project.jar guard of ako/mxcli#2640 (d43db2c1, merged the day before) counted any entry whose CRC or size changed as new Java. Mendix generates a call stub per microflow in each module's proxies/microflows/Microflows class, and on 11.15/11.16 the attach's build (the dev loop's incremental build, then a cold one on a private serve because web/dist lost its pages) recompiles it, so the injected test microflow changes mxtest/proxies/microflows/Microflows.class. The guard's comment assumed the injection adds no Java. The test needs a cached mxbuild and a runtime, so only the nightly runs it
insight: Measure what changed before deciding what a change means: a diagnostic build of the guard printing the differing entries showed exactly one, `mxtest/proxies/microflows/Microflows.class` 860 -> 1128 bytes, of 163. A microflow proxy is no Java the running runtime needs (it runs microflows by name, and the test endpoint calls Core.microflowCall); only Java calling the new stub would need it, and that Java is a changed class of its own, which the comparison still sees. When a guard gates the attach, run the attach integration test on every prebuilt-client version (11.14-11.17) before merging. Controls: the unit test's proxy-only case fails with the filter stubbed (changed=true); the integration test with the fix passes on 11.16.0 and 11.15.0 (the failing legs) and on 11.17.0
